questions.question: The concept of biodiversity hotspots, defined as regions with very high species richness, high endemism and severe threat, was proposed by:

solution.key_concept: Biodiversity hotspots were proposed by Norman Myers.
steps: Hotspots are regions with very high species richness, high endemism and a high degree of threat.
This concept was put forward by Norman Myers.
solution.why_not_others: Paul Ehrlich, Alexander von Humboldt and David Tilman are known for other ideas in ecology. None of them proposed the hotspot concept.
solution.common_trap: Students may confuse ecologists who are known for other biodiversity concepts with the person who proposed hotspots.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the word 'hotspots' directly to Myers.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ex situ conservation?
options: Cryopreservation of gametes in liquid nitrogen at $-196^{\circ}C$
Protection of forest patches as sacred groves

solution.key_concept: Ex situ conservation protects organisms away from their natural habitat.
steps: Ex situ methods include zoos, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, cryopreservation, in vitro fertilisation, tissue culture and seed banks.
Gametes can be kept viable for long periods in liquid nitrogen at $-196^{\circ}C$.
Sacred groves, national parks and biosphere reserves protect species within their natural habitats, so they are in situ.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Cryopreservation of gametes in liquid nitrogen at $-196^{\circ}C$
solution.why_not_others: Options 2, 3 and 4 all protect organisms in their natural habitats, so they are in situ methods.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that every human-managed protected area is ex situ.
solution.time_saving_tip: Ask whether the organism has been removed from its habitat. If it has, the method is ex situ.

questions.question: Biodiversity hotspots cover less than a certain fraction of Earth's land area, and their strict protection could reduce ongoing mass extinctions by a certain amount. Which pair is correct?
options: Less than 30% of land area; extinctions reduced by about 2%
Less than 10% of land area; extinctions reduced by about 30%
Less than 2% of land area; extinctions reduced by about 10%
Less than 2% of land area; extinctions reduced by about 30%

solution.key_concept: Hotspots are small in area but very valuable for conservation.
steps: All hotspots together cover less than 2% of Earth's land area.
Strict protection of these hotspots could reduce ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30%.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Less than 2% of land area; extinctions reduced by about 30%
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the two figures. Option 2 gives the wrong land area. Option 3 gives the wrong reduction in extinctions.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the pairing: a small area (2%) gives a large benefit (30%).

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: India's rich biodiversity regions are covered by four of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
statements.R: Biodiversity hotspots are identified on the basis of high species richness, high endemism and a high degree of threat.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: India's rich biodiversity regions fall within three hotspots, and hotspots are identified by three criteria.
steps: India's rich biodiversity regions are covered by three hotspots: the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and the Himalaya.
Assertion A says four hotspots, so A is false.
The hotspot criteria are high species richness, high endemism and high threat, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Counting Western Ghats and Sri Lanka as two separate hotspots.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember 34 hotspots worldwide and 3 that cover India.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: At the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Johannesburg in 2002, 190 countries pledged to significantly reduce the current rate of biodiversity loss by 2010.
statements.II: The number of biodiversity hotspots, originally 25, has now risen to 34, and together they cover less than 2% of Earth's land area.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: This tests facts about international conservation efforts and hotspot statistics.
steps: Johannesburg 2002: 190 countries pledged to significantly reduce biodiversity loss by 2010. Statement I is correct.
Hotspots were originally 25 and now number 34, covering less than 2% of land area. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Every figure in both statements matches the facts: 190 countries, 2010, 25, 34 and 2%. So no option that marks a statement incorrect can be right.
solution.common_trap: Confusing Johannesburg 2002 with the Rio Earth Summit 1992, which produced the Convention on Biological Diversity.
solution.time_saving_tip: Check every number in each statement against the facts you remember.

questions.question: In a biosphere reserve, the zone in which no human activity is permitted is the:

solution.key_concept: A biosphere reserve has three zones with increasing levels of human activity.
steps: The core zone allows no human activity.
The buffer zone allows limited research and education.
The transition (manipulation) zone allows human settlement and activities.
solution.why_not_others: The buffer zone permits limited research and education. The transition zone, also called the manipulation zone, permits human settlement and activities.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the buffer zone is fully protected.
solution.time_saving_tip: Human activity increases as you move from the core, to the buffer, to the transition zone.

questions.question: A protected area in which harvesting of timber and collection of minor forest products are permitted, provided they do not harm the animals, is a:
options: Core zone of a biosphere reserve

solution.key_concept: Wildlife sanctuaries permit limited human activities.
steps: National parks give strict protection, with no grazing, cultivation, private ownership or forestry.
Wildlife sanctuaries protect animals but allow timber harvesting and collection of minor forest products if these do not harm the animals.
solution.why_not_others: National parks and the core zone of a biosphere reserve do not allow such activities. A seed bank is an ex situ facility, not a protected area.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember: national park means no human activity, while a sanctuary allows limited activity.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly gives the number of in situ protected areas in India?
options: 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries
90 biosphere reserves, 14 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries
14 biosphere reserves, 448 national parks and 90 wildlife sanctuaries
34 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries

solution.key_concept: These are India's figures for in situ protected areas.
steps: India has 14 biosphere reserves.
India has 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 3 interchange the figures. Option 4 uses 34, which is the number of global biodiversity hotspots.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the number of hotspots (34) with the number of biosphere reserves (14).
solution.time_saving_tip: Sanctuaries far outnumber national parks, so the largest figure, 448, belongs to sanctuaries.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_I.label: D
list_I.text: Madhya Pradesh (as listed in the standard account)

solution.key_concept: Sacred groves are found in specific regions of India.
steps: Meghalaya: Khasi and Jaintia Hills (A-III).
Rajasthan: Aravalli Hills (B-I).
Karnataka and Maharashtra: Western Ghats region (C-IV).
Madhya Pradesh: Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas (D-II). Sarguja and Bastar are now in Chhattisgarh.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the Meghalaya and Rajasthan regions. Option 2 swaps the Aravalli Hills and the Western Ghats. Option 4 swaps the Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh regions.
solution.common_trap: Placing the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Rajasthan, or placing Bastar in Meghalaya.
solution.time_saving_tip: The Aravalli Hills belong only to Rajasthan, so fix B-I first and eliminate options.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about in situ conservation are correct?

statements.A: Biosphere reserves are multipurpose protected areas under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme.
statements.B: The buffer zone of a biosphere reserve is the area where human settlement and cultivation are allowed.
statements.C: National parks do not permit grazing, private ownership or forestry.
statements.D: Sacred groves are an ex situ method of conservation managed by botanical gardens.
statements.E: Sacred groves serve as refuges for many rare and threatened plants.

solution.key_concept: This tests the features of biosphere reserves, national parks and sacred groves.
steps: A is correct: biosphere reserves come under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere programme.
B is incorrect: human settlement is allowed in the transition zone. The buffer zone allows only limited research and education.
C is correct: national parks forbid grazing, cultivation, private ownership and forestry.
D is incorrect: sacred groves are in situ conservation protected by tribal communities on religious grounds.
E is correct: sacred groves shelter rare and threatened plants.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes B, and option 2 includes D, both of which are incorrect. Option 3 leaves out the correct statement E.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the buffer zone with the transition zone, and calling sacred groves ex situ.
solution.time_saving_tip: First eliminate the clearly false statements B and D. Only option 4 then contains all of A, C and E.
